purpose: Editorially selected Signals candidates for the Sunday 9 August 2026 edition. Only the URLs below may be promoted; each promoted row receives final editorial significance before publication.

topics.editorialRationale: Select OpenAI's explicit disclosure that it cannot rule out critical cyber capabilities in an upcoming model. It makes model-access controls, evaluation governance and intervention evidence an immediate executive issue rather than generic AI commentary.
Select ESMA's T+1 readiness statement because it turns the 2027 transition into a dated 2026 operating programme across allocations, confirmations and the full settlement chain.
No new third-party candidate is promoted. Retain the reviewed current evidence rather than relabelling an already-covered cloud incident as a fresh development.
No new resilience candidate is promoted. The NCSC response is valuable context for the AI capability story, but is not duplicated as a separate public signal.

Select OFSI's 6 August amendment to a Russia-related general licence. It is a specific current sanctions-control signal: firms need to identify whether a changed permission affects counterparties or activity, then retain a versioned applicability and decision record.
Select CISA's newly added known-exploited vulnerability because active exploitation is a direct test of asset visibility, patch prioritisation, exception governance and recovery evidence.
No new technology-failure candidate is promoted. Retain the reviewed failure and recovery evidence rather than promoting an already-covered incident.
Select the ICO enforcement notice because it provides a current, accountable data-governance read-across on security, records, retention and remedial evidence.
